title: Microsoft Teams: keypad consent for recording and transcription in one-to-one PSTN calls
summary: Hold: the consent behaviour, rollout information and calling-policy controls are supported, but the audit control needs correction. Microsoft documents audit search automation that the table reports as absent, and the Purview instructions omit the Audit and Search navigation steps.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Microsoft Teams plans keypad consent for recording and transcription in one-to-one PSTN calls.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams will support explicit consent for participants connected through the public switched telephone network (PSTN) in one-to-one calls.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the keypad prompt for this one-to-one PSTN capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams one-to-one PSTN keypad consent recording transcription press 1 2 ExplicitRecordingConsent PSTN only policy. Opened call-recording-transcription-captions and participant-agreement-recording-transcription; keypad results concern Audio Conferencing, not this capability.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The call-recording Learn page describes a Yes or No consent prompt for call participants.
claims.quote: When a participant decides to un-mute, turn on their camera, or share content, they’re asked to respond 'Yes' or 'No' to consent to be included in the recording and transcription.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].governs; Governance controls
claims.claim: The calling-policy ExplicitRecordingConsent parameter covers both Teams one-to-one VoIP and PSTN calls, rather than only PSTN calls.
claims.quote: This parameter manages recording consent for Teams 1:1 VoIP and PSTN calls.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The meeting-consent Learn page currently lists PSTN endpoints in one-to-one calls as auto-consented endpoints.
claims.quote: The following user types are auto consented for recording and transcription without any participant interaction. ... PSTN endpoints in 1:1 calls

claims.claim: The consent requirement is admin-opt-in through the existing calling-policy setting.
claims.quote: The existing explicit consent setting is disabled by default. ... If your organization wants to require explicit consent, enable the existing setting in the appropriate calling policies.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Capability-specific licensing and metering are not yet published, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN explicit recording consent licensing Teams Phone license keypad. Opened teams-phone-licensing, teams-calling-policy and call-recording-transcription-captions; no capability-specific licence or meter found. General Teams Phone licensing is documented.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor the supplied notice names a licence, meter or charge for this capability.
claims.quote: This capability uses the existing explicit consent setting in Teams calling policies. It does not introduce a new admin policy setting.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The calling-policies Learn page describes the consent setting without naming a licence for it.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN explicit recording consent licensing Teams Phone license keypad. Opened and read teams-calling-policy in full, including Calling policy settings; it names no licence for Require participant agreement for recording and transcription.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The consent UI is Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Edit > Require participant agreement for recording and transcription.
claims.quote: select Voice > Calling policies. ... Select the policy or policies that you want to modify, and then select Edit. ... Require participant agreement for recording and transcription

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell documents Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExplicitRecordingConsent <string> for the calling policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy ... [-Identity] <string> ... [-ExplicitRecordingConsent <string>] ... This setting controls whether users must provide or obtain explicit consent before recording a 1:1 PSTN or Teams call.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The cmdlet reference marks ExplicitRecordingConsent as not released and ineffective when enabled or disabled, unlike the existing-setting description in the notice and call-recording page.
claims.quote: This feature has not been released yet and will have no changes if it is enabled or disabled.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate PSTN-only or keypad-only consent switch on either admin UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams one-to-one PSTN keypad consent recording transcription press 1 2 ExplicitRecordingConsent PSTN only policy; Teams PSTN ExplicitRecordingConsent only. Opened teams-calling-policy, call-recording-transcription-captions and Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy; only the shared setting is documented.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Cloud recording for calling controls whether a user's one-to-one Teams or PSTN call can be recorded.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Voice > Calling policies. ... Select the policy that you want to edit. ... Turn Cloud recording for calling to On.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowCloudRecordingForCalls $true enables call recording for the global policy.
claims.quote: For example, this script enables call recording for the global policy: ... Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowCloudRecordingForCalls $true

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Transcription controls whether users can transcribe calls, separately from consent.
claims.quote: To turn on call transcription for users: ... In the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Voice > Calling policies. ... Select the policy you want to modify. ... Turn Transcription to On.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true enables transcription for the global policy.
claims.quote: For example, this script enables transcription for the global policy: ... Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true

claims.where: controls[4].api; Governance controls table and closing prose
claims.claim: Automation for reviewing call consent audit data is not yet documented.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog. That means you can use this cmdlet to search the audit log instead of using the search tool on the Audit page in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.fix: Populate controls[4].api with Exchange Online PowerShell: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <start date> -EndDate <end date> -Operations CallParticipantDetail; docs https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/search-unifiedauditlog. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-activities#teams-activities for the mapping from Added information about call participants to CallParticipantDetail. Replace the broad no-API statement; retain the caveat that PSTN keypad consent logging is unconfirmed.

claims.where: controls[4].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Teams calling audit logs > Added information about call participants filter is the admin navigation path.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable: ... Activities - friendly names: Select the drop-down list to display the friendly names for audited activities that you can search for.
claims.fix: Replace the descriptive pseudo-path with Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search > Activities - friendly names > Added information about call participants. Use https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-search as the navigation reference and also cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-activities#teams-activities for the activity name. Keep the existing call-recording citation for consent applicability, and instruct readers to set a date range and select Search.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The supplied notice describes phone-keypad interaction and does not describe a sign-in step.
claims.quote: When explicit consent is required, PSTN participants will hear an audio prompt when recording or transcription starts and can use their phone keypad to consent or decline.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The described capability involves participants choosing consent, not autonomous actions.
claims.quote: They can use their phone keypad to consent or decline. Participants who decline can remain in the call but stay muted.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy reference defines Disabled as not requiring users to obtain explicit consent before recording starts.
claims.quote: Disabled: Users are not required to obtain explicit consent before recording starts.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Calling policies are assigned to users, so different assigned policies can produce different consent requirements.
claims.quote: You can use the global (Org-wide default) policy that's created automatically or create and assign custom policies. ... When this is on, participants must agree to be recorded and transcribed.

claims.where: Scope
claims.claim: Learn says Audio Conferencing and group calls use the Teams meeting policy instead of the calling-policy consent parameter.
claims.quote: Audio conferencing and group calls are managed by Teams Meeting Policy.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to check which users receive a calling policy, but the controls table has no policy-assignment row.
claims.quote: Check that those policies are assigned to the intended users, especially staff who take external phone calls. ... Whether participants must agree to recording and transcription in 1:1 calls, including PSTN ... Reviewing call consent data in the audit log
claims.fix: Add a controls row for which users receive each Teams calling policy, documenting policy assignment, or remove the separate checklist instruction to check assignments. The existing cited https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-calling-policy describes assignment options and links to assignment instructions.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The new keypad experience affects applicable one-to-one PSTN calls where explicit consent is required, rather than calls whose consent setting remains disabled.
claims.quote: PSTN participants in applicable one-to-one Teams calls where explicit consent for recording or transcription is required ... If explicit consent is already enabled, prepare users and support teams for the new PSTN keypad consent experience.
